title: Introduce workspace/ authoring layer and two-layer architecture (Phase 1)
rationale: The repository had no separation between the authoring/workshop layer and the public publication layer. All files (HTML, canonical graph JSON, patch files, audit documents, migration scripts, and public site assets) were co-located at the root level with no organizational structure. This created several concrete problems: (1) The patch file inventory (13+ JSON files at root) had no application log — it was unknown which were already incorporated into v96 and which were pending. (2) The scripts/ directory existed but had no README or documented lifecycle. (3) No machine-readable status model existed — only 13/2,263 entities had any status-like attribute. (4) No DecisionTrace infrastructure existed; decisions were only captured in informal Markdown audit docs. (5) NarrativePreset management was absent despite narrative-anchors-build.mjs already functioning. Phase 1 introduces workspace/ as the authoring layer and public/exports/ as the publication output target, following a local-first, file-first, non-destructive architecture.
author: mael-rolland.eth
consequences: Phase 2: audit and consolidate root patch files into workspace/patches/
Phase 2: move docs/ audit documents to workspace/audits/
Phase 2: produce grc20-these-mael-rolland-v97.json via validated patch application
notes: Phase 1 constraints strictly observed: no HTML/CSS/JS files modified, no canonical graph JSON modified, no package.json changes, no file moves from existing locations, no runtime behavior changes. All new files are additive. The pre-existing scripts/ directory at repository root was NOT modified — its boundary with workspace/scripts/ is documented in workspace/scripts/README.md. The public/exports/ directory is empty and not referenced by any public-facing code.
